lines.say: The test: the same apartheid definition used on Israel.
About 88 percent of people living in Qatar are not citizens.
Become a citizen? Live there 25 years. Then, no more than 50 people a year.
Change jobs? For years, workers needed their employer's permission. Reforms came in 2020. Vote? Non-citizens never could. In 2024, even citizens voted to end their elections.
By the same definition used on Israel: is this apartheid? You decide.
Israel: one in five citizens is Arab. They vote. Arab parties won 19 seats. Arab judges sit on the Supreme Court.
Qatar is rarely called apartheid. Israel is called it daily. Both have real problems. One standard.
So, let's run the test again.

vis.text: institutionalized regime of systematic oppression and domination

note.text: Amnesty International (2022) and Human Rights Watch (2021) applied this definition to Israel.
2020: about 88% of 2.85 million residents were non-Qatari (GLMM estimate from official data).
Qatar Nationality Law 38 of 2005: 25 years residence (art. 2), cap of 50 a year (art. 17).
Employer permission dropped in 2020 (ILO). Nov 2024 referendum ended Shura Council elections.
Israel: about 21% of citizens are Arab (CBS, 2025). 19 Arab party seats (Oct 2026). Justice Kabub (2022).

caption_en:
Qatar, judged like Israel. Ready? 🇶🇦

Same test, same definition: the one Amnesty (2022) and Human Rights Watch (2021) use on Israel. The Rome Statute calls apartheid an "institutionalized regime of systematic oppression and domination". Real facts only:

1. About 88% of Qatar's 2.85 million residents were not citizens in 2020 (GLMM estimate from official data).
2. Nationality Law 38 of 2005: 25 years of residence to apply (art. 2), and no more than 50 new citizens a year (art. 17).
3. For years, migrant workers needed their employer's permission to change jobs. Qatar dropped that in 2020 and set a minimum wage (ILO).
4. Non-citizens have never voted. In November 2024, citizens voted 90.6% to end Shura Council elections.

By the same definition used on Israel: is this apartheid? You decide.

Israel: about 21% of citizens are Arab. They vote, Arab parties won 19 Knesset seats in October 2026, and Justice Khaled Kabub has sat on the Supreme Court since 2022. Israel has real problems too.

Qatar is rarely called apartheid. Israel is called it daily. One standard.
caption_he: קטאר, אם היו בודקים אותה כמו את ישראל, לפי אותה הגדרת אפרטהייד שאמנסטי וארגון Human Rights Watch מפעילים על ישראל. עובדות בלבד: כ-88% מתושבי קטאר אינם אזרחים. כדי לבקש אזרחות צריך 25 שנות מגורים, ולא יותר מ-50 אזרחים חדשים בשנה. במשך שנים עובדים זרים היו צריכים אישור מהמעסיק כדי להחליף עבודה, עד הרפורמה של 2020. מי שאינו אזרח מעולם לא הצביע, וב-2024 גם האזרחים הצביעו לבטל את הבחירות למועצת השורא. לפי אותה הגדרה, האם זה אפרטהייד? תחליטו אתם. בישראל כ-21% מהאזרחים ערבים, הם מצביעים, המפלגות הערביות זכו ב-19 מושבים, ושופט ערבי יושב בבית המשפט העליון. גם לישראל יש בעיות אמיתיות. אותו סטנדרט לכולן.
